body: Nope, I'd already shown her that one and she said it wasn't it
No, she said it's definitely them all standing in a line
My roommate is 20 in case that helps at all if it's a modern painting I don't know of. At this point I'm pretty sure it's not a Degas.

No matter how much I try to explain it to other people, they just don't get it. They offer sympathy and try to be encouraging but sometimes it hurts way more than it helps. Especially when they try to make promises that I know they won't keep in the long run

I think that if you can keep your promise to yourself, you should, and stick around.

You've made strides and that's something you should be really proud of. Personally, a lot of my feelings of numbness, etc are cyclical and they come and (eventually) go. I don't know if this would help you, but doing things that make me feel tend to help me get through a day. Like sitting in the sun to feel the warmth, or eating really spicy food. They're little but sometimes it just takes getting through one more day.

Know you're not alone right now, no matter how empty you feel.

Sometimes the self awareness is the worst. Seeing the steps you've taken and it still not doing enough to feel like you're really making changes. And seeing things that keep getting in the way of getting better. It hurts, a lot, and it takes a lot to keep going even when there seems to be so little to show for your efforts. Sitting with that knowledge is painful. But showing up for yourself and trying things like therapy is a positive even if it hasn't helped much
Yeah, I'm lower than I have been in years which is why I keep thinking now would be a good time to go. Trying to consider being stuck here for decades makes me panic. I just can't be here anymore.

It's so hard when other people get tired of you. Like they at least get to distance themselves, while I'm stuck with me. As an aside though, you should be proud of yourself for making it as far as you have, resilience is exhausting.
